summary: Hong Sieng Kong is a restored riverside warehouse compound in Talat Noi, with antique-filled rooms, a garden and outdoor seating beside the Chao Phraya. It makes a memorable café stop during a neighbourhood walk; the setting is the main draw, while food and service reviews are mixed.
whyGo: Explore a cluster of old warehouses adapted as a café while keeping their historic character.
Take a shaded pause with river views, indoor antique displays and outdoor seating.
Pair it with Talat Noi lanes and nearby Chinese shrines rather than making a special cross-city trip just for coffee.
bestFor: Walkers wanting a scenic rest in Talat Noi
Visitors who value atmosphere and photography over destination dining
skipIf: You want a quiet, low-cost café without a purchase expectation or tourist crowds.
You need a fully audited step-free route or consistent table service.
You are choosing primarily for outstanding food; recent visitor feedback is mixed.
duration: Allow 45–90 minutes for a drink or light meal and a look around; this is a planning estimate. Combine with a 1–2 hour Talat Noi walk if exploring the area.
cost: No admission fee is listed, but plan to buy at least one item per person to use the seated areas: visitor reports describe this policy, though it is not confirmed on the venue page. An older Thai directory quotes roughly ฿100–250 for menu items; treat that as a loose estimate and check the current menu.
hours: Listings commonly show Tuesday–Sunday, 10:00–20:00, closed Monday. Time Out Thailand’s page has conflicting hours in its detail fields, so call +66 95 998 9895 or check the venue’s Facebook page before going.
bestTime: Late afternoon gives softer light and a chance to enjoy the river terrace; arrive earlier on weekends if you want a choice of seats. Midday is useful as a shaded break, though outdoor areas may still feel hot.
gettingThere: Address: 734–736 Soi Wanit 2, Talat Noi, Samphanthawong. Time Out advises against asking a taxi to reach the door because the lanes are narrow; walk in from a convenient Talat Noi or Chinatown drop-off and explore the neighbourhood. Check a live map for the best route from your starting point.
booking: No reservation requirement was found. For a group or a specific seating area, contact the café at +66 95 998 9895 or through its Facebook page; confirm holiday hours and the current minimum purchase policy.
accessibility: No formal accessibility information was found. The approach uses narrow neighbourhood lanes, and the compound is a converted historic building with multiple indoor and outdoor spaces. Step-free access, accessible toilets and seating access are unverified; contact the venue before visiting if these are essential.
practicalTips: Follow the venue’s order process at the entrance and ask staff where guests may sit before exploring the compound.
Bring cash as a backup; payment methods were not confirmed from a primary source.
Expect a self-service style at busy times according to recent visitor reviews.
Ask before photographing staff, residents or private areas, and keep narrow lanes clear.
decemberNotes: A useful cool-season pause during a Talat Noi walk, with the river terrace especially appealing in late afternoon. December 2026 holiday or special-event hours have not been announced in the sources checked; confirm directly, particularly around Christmas and New Year. No venue-specific December event was verified.
uncertainties: Opening-time listings conflict in their closing time; 20:00 is the common current listing, but reconfirm directly.
Current menu prices, payment methods and the per-person purchase policy were not verified from the venue itself.
Accessibility details and December 2026 holiday hours are unpublished in the sources checked.
